candidate_text:
I know that my distress will become my deliverance through your prayers and the generous help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ. I eagerly expect and hope that I will have no reason to be ashamed. Instead, I will face this with complete courage so that Christ will be honored through me, whether I live or die.

For me, living is Christ, and dying is gain. If I go on living, I can continue doing fruitful work. I do not know which I would prefer. I am pulled in both directions. I long to leave this life and be with Christ, which is far better. But remaining alive is more necessary for your sake.

Since I am convinced of this, I know that I will remain and continue with all of you for your progress and joy as you trust Christ. Then, when I am with you again, you will have even more reason to rejoice in Christ Jesus because of me.

warrant_checker.evidence: No broad commentary layer or unrelated explanatory material is introduced.
Captures the ample/provision sense of ἐπιχορηγία but adds evaluative warmth.

communication_readability_checker.evidence: Candidate uses current vocabulary, explicit referents, and manageable sentence structure for the target reader.

discourse_cohesion_checker.evidence: Major logical and rhetorical progression of the source unit remains visible.
The pull between fruitful ministry and being with Christ remains clear.

theological_risk_checker.evidence: Candidate preserves ambiguity between release/vindication/final salvation by retaining “deliverance.”

ambiguity_scope_checker.evidence: “My distress” identifies the referent dynamically; defensible, but more specific than “this.”

checker_independence_note: Procedural role separation only; same assistant environment.
